principles: Unreleased SoCs receive probabilistic priors, never fixed winner labels.
Priors must distinguish peak performance, sustained performance, power efficiency, thermals, modem/RF and workload class.
Current-generation evidence can shift priors for successors, but uncertainty must remain wider than for released silicon.
Architecture/process rumors are supporting evidence only until silicon measurements exist.
Do not collapse multiple current Qualcomm flagship tiers into one baseline when they have different clocks, thermal envelopes, or OEM positioning.

rationale: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is Qualcomm's highest-performance Gen 6 tier, with Oryon prime cores up to 5 GHz and therefore should be modeled separately from regular Elite Gen 6.
Exynos 2600 already demonstrated strong sustained synthetic stability in some workloads, creating a legitimate prior for Samsung to prioritize sustained efficiency again.
Any Exynos 2700 advantage remains speculative until measured silicon exists.
Rumored process/power improvements for Exynos 2700 are supporting evidence only and must not override future measurements.
Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 shares Qualcomm's 2 nm generation and Oryon architecture but is positioned below Elite Extreme Gen 6.

Because it is the less aggressive Qualcomm flagship tier, Exynos 2700 has a stronger prior chance of matching or exceeding sustained efficiency and long-run performance than against Elite Extreme Gen 6.
This remains a prior, not a released-silicon conclusion.
